author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India’s foreign-exchange reserves reached a record $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, rising by nearly $45 billion from the prior week, central-bank data released Friday showed.

The reserve pool has increased for 10 consecutive weeks and gained almost $120 billion over that span. The Reserve Bank of India attracted $136.3 billion between June 5 and August 31 through measures designed to bring in dollars, including discounted hedging for overseas borrowing and no-cost hedging for banks raising foreign-currency deposits.

Non-resident Indian deposits accounted for $127 billion of the inflows. In the latest week, foreign-currency assets rose by $47.4 billion while the value of gold holdings fell by about $2.6 billion to $113.8 billion.

The larger buffer can strengthen India’s ability to manage currency volatility and external shocks. Bankers told Reuters that intervention to support the rupee likely absorbed some inflows, while analysts noted that hedged deposits also create future obligations in the central bank’s forward book.
dek: Central-bank data show reserves rose by nearly $45 billion in a week after policy measures drew large overseas inflows.
headline: India’s foreign-exchange reserves jump to record $785.7 billion
